assets.name: Finger-Mice Colony

canonical.anatomy: Knucklebones scurry in groups of five, assembling a hand only when threatened. No joint explains the motion; instead five separate trails curl toward one center point.
canonical.locomotion: Its bodies move by passing one impulse through the whole colony; the permission cue is five separate trails curl toward one center point.
canonical.sound: Gnawed relic produces many dry contacts resolving into a single synchronized beat; Make a Fist commits on the first strike sound after the gap.
canonical.purpose: Small scavengers assemble borrowed skeletons into increasingly ambitious communal bodies; this colony uses five scurrying knucklebone groups that assemble a hand only when threatened.
canonical.origin: Knucklebones scurry in groups of five, assembling a hand only when threatened.
canonical.cue: Five separate trails curl toward one center point.
canonical.counterplay: Scatter the fingers with area damage before the fist closes.

assets.masterDirection: Show one complete Finger-Mice Colony as EXACTLY FIVE separately countable finger-shaped knucklebone organisms, each a mature unsettling chain of small borrowed finger joints and cracked enamel rather than a cute mouse, ordinary hand, or humanoid skeleton. The five units are still separate but are converging to assemble one incomplete hand/fist at a single hollow center. From each unit, exactly one thin pale tooth-dust and mold-ligament motion trail curls inward toward that same center, making EXACTLY FIVE separate trails; no trails merge before the center. Arrange the units at five distinct stages of one synchronized inward impulse so the imminent fist closure is readable but not complete, leaving clear gaps where area damage can scatter them. Treat all five units and trails as one colony subject. Keep every unit and every trail fully inside frame and separated against black.
